records.quote: the first thing I set to work to do was to try to discover whereabouts the brutes lay up for the day
records.paraphrase: Quatermain describes deliberately investigating where the lions rested.

records.quote: One letter only have I received from the old gentleman, dated from a mission station high up the Tana, a river on the east coast, about three hundred miles north of Zanzibar.
records.paraphrase: The narrator locates Quatermain's last message at a specific remote African location.

records.quote: there I lay shaking with terror, and the cold perspiration pouring out of me, feeling like another Daniel come to judgment in a new sense of the phrase
records.paraphrase: Quatermain describes his terror while lions fed near him.

records.quote: I have been lame ever since, and shall be to my dying day; in the month of March the wound always troubles me a great deal, and every three years it breaks out raw.
records.paraphrase: Quatermain describes the lasting physical consequences of his lion wound.

records.quote: I opened the breech of the gun and hurriedly pulled out the old case, which, to judge from what ensued, must, I suppose, have burst and left a portion of its fabric sticking to the barrel. At any rate, when I tried to get in the new cartridge it would only enter half-way
records.paraphrase: Quatermain explains the technical cause of his gun jamming: a burst cartridge case fouling the barrel.

records.quote: there was a strong wind blowing from the direction of the waggon, across the reedy pan towards the bush-clad kloof or donga, and this first gave me the idea of firing the reeds, which, as I think I told you, were pretty dry
records.paraphrase: Quatermain explains how wind direction and dry reeds informed his plan to drive the lions out by fire.

records.quote: Shortly after that, the death of his only son so unsettled him that he immediately left England, accompanied by two companions, his old fellow-voyagers, Sir Henry Curtis and Captain Good, and has now utterly vanished into the dark heart of Africa.
records.paraphrase: The narrator explains that Quatermain, grieving his son's death, departed for Africa and disappeared.

records.quote: Those people carry the doctrine of the survival of the fittest to its extreme, you see.
records.paraphrase: Quatermain frames the abandonment of the old woman in terms of survival of the fittest.

records.quote: she told me that all the people whom I had seen had died of fever. When they had died the other inhabitants of the kraal had taken the cattle and gone away, leaving the poor old woman, who was helpless from age and infirmity, to perish of starvation or disease
records.paraphrase: An entire kraal's inhabitants died of fever, and the survivors abandoned an old woman to die.

records.quote: I took the smoothbore because it shot a bullet very well; and my experience has been that a round ball from a smoothbore is quite as effective against a lion as an express bullet. The lion is soft, and not a difficult animal to finish if you hit him anywhere in the body. A buck takes far more killing.
records.paraphrase: Quatermain explains his technical reasoning for choosing a smoothbore and how lions differ from bucks in vulnerability.

criteria.rationale: The single phrase invoking 'survival of the fittest' is a rhetorical, ironic aside about local custom, and the ballistic remarks are practical hunting lore rather than any materially represented scientific fact, theory, discovery, or natural process central to the story. No speculative or genuine science drives the narrative.

The smoothbore breechloader and jammed cartridge are ordinary 19th-century firearms functioning as everyday hunting tools; there is no engineered novum or invention that speculatively affects the setting. This is a period adventure, not a technology-driven premise.

The tale is set in a specified historical past (March 1869) in an ordinary geographic region of Africa, with no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement. A dated real location is an incidental historical setting, not a speculative time element.

The lasting lameness is a personal physical consequence of an injury, not consequences systematically developed from an identifiable scientific, technological, social, or historical premise. No extrapolative reasoning structures the narrative.

Quatermain deliberately investigates the lions' lair, reads tracks and kill remains as evidence, and reasons about wind direction and dry reeds to devise a fire plan. This is systematic inference and observation driving action, but it is ordinary woodcraft/hunting deduction rather than formal scientific method, so materiality and interpretation are uncertain.
All action occurs in ordinary terrestrial Africa. There are no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them.

A pervasive fever epidemic that wiped out an entire kraal and haunts the region is a remembered biological disaster of some scale, giving it possible catastrophe standing. However, it is background atmosphere rather than causally central to the lion-hunt plot, so materiality is uncertain.

candidates.description: A rumored hidden white people existing somewhere in the unexplored African interior, which Quatermain believes in and quests to find.

novelty.rationale: A hidden lost civilization could constitute a world-altering difference from the empirical norm (an unknown people in unexplored regions), but the story only mentions it as an unverified rumor in the framing preface; it is never confirmed to exist within the storyworld, leaving its ontological status unresolved.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The text provides no systematic or immanent account of such a people; it is only alluded to as rumor with no supporting evidence in the supplied set.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The rumored hidden people appears only in the framing device and is entirely disconnected from the actual narrative, which is a self-contained lion-hunting adventure recollection. It does not govern the story's logic.

estrangement.rationale: The framing narrator gestures toward an unexplored interior harboring an unknown people, contrasting the mapped colonial world with a mysterious blank space, but this remains a marginal rumor rather than a realized estrangement.

candidates.description: The lion family encounter and hunt that forms the core of Quatermain's recollected adventure.

novelty.rationale: Lions, hunting, guns, and fever in colonial Africa are all consistent with the empirical historical norm of the setting; nothing here totalizes or alters the story universe.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The narrative is presented with coherent, mundane realism and detailed technical reasoning about firearms, ballistics, wind, and fire; but this is ordinary realism, not an imaginary or novel cognitive framework.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The lion hunt does drive the entire embedded narrative, but as a realistic adventure event, not as a novum-based world-altering premise.

estrangement.rationale: The danger and physical consequences are vivid but belong to ordinary adventure realism, offering no cognitive estrangement from an empirical norm.
